newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London slip, eye FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London slip, eye FOMC meeting.

text.p: Hong Kong shares slipped back in London as U.S. interest rate worries kept investors sidelined and a large placing in the market knocked prices across the board, traders said.
The placing of 55 million shares in Henderson Land at HK$64 unsettled a thin market, the stock falling to HK$64-1/2 in mid-afternoon. Henderson shares closed in Hong Kong at HK$66-1/4.
"That pulled the rest of the market down with it and with the knock-on effect of the weak UK market we're lower across the board," said one trader.
"Everyone is really on the sidelines waiting for the U.S. Fed move tomorrow," he added.
By 1357 GMT the Hang Seng London Reference index was down 90,80 points at 11,531.33.
Overnight in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index hit a new 1996 intraday high of 11,684.00. The index slipped back to finish at 11,622.13, a gain of 29.77 on the session.
Traders said a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates, expected at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting (FOMC) had largely been discounted by the market.
